title.narrative: Assist crisis-affected people in Myanmar to meet their food and nutrition needs

description.narrative: WFP aims to bolster delivery of its comprehensive humanitarian response to address the needs of crisis-affected people in Myanmar with CERF support to this underfunded emergency. WFP will use USD 2 million in CERF funds to provide life-saving cash assistance to 62,000 people across the country to help reduce food insecurity. The key objectives for WFP include: 1. Empower People in Need: To provide people with the flexibility and agency to prioritise their own needs based on their individual circumstances and preferences through the provision of unrestricted cash transfers. These transfers will enable WFP beneficiaries to make their own choices about how to allocate resources, addressing a range of critical needs such as food, health, WASH, and shelter. This approach fosters a sense of empowerment, reduces deprivation, and promotes resilience. 2. Promote Localisation: To support the localization of humanitarian assistance in Myanmar, WFP will continue to work closely with local partners. WFP will channel the assistance and operating resources through and to local partners so they can reach people in need in the field, while WFP also provides support to strengthen their capacity. This approach to localization and working with local partners, will help ensure that humanitarian assistance is delivered in an effective and dignified manner, building local ownership and sustainability. 3. Mainstream Protection: WFP will also pursue its goal of operational effectiveness through the mainstreaming of protection standards into all aspects of WFP project design and implementation. This will help ensure that the right people receive the right entitlements at the right time in a safe and dignified manner that minimises risk. WFP will prioritize on: 1. Multipurpose Cash (MPC) to support the short-term emergency response In alignment with planning for the 2025 Myanmar Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan, WFP will provide multi-sectoral, multipurpose cash to about 17,000 people across 4,000 households for up to 2 months. This timely, short-term emergency response will help people in all their diversity meet their immediate and evolving needs and priorities. This approach prioritizes a timely rapid response, targeting people on a household basis, and avoids the need for household-level individual registration. 2. Food Security – WFP emergency relief cash assistance WFP will provide unconditional cash transfers to about 45,000 people affected by crisis to address their immediate food security needs. WFP plans to reach the 45,000 people with one month of cash assistance. WFP will aim to increase inclusive and meaningful participation of people with specific protection needs, including persons with disabilities and nutritionally vulnerable individuals through cash top-up payments. WFP will channel its cash transfers through local community-based organization (CBO) and non-government organisation (NGO) partners acting as the transfer agents in the absence of formal financial service providers. 3. Protection Mainstreaming WFP is dedicated to ensuring protection and accountability to affected populations across its programmes.
